definition: to increase suddenly and by a large amount
exampleIELTS: Online sales surged from 12% in 2010 to 38% in 2020, overtaking in-store purchases.

definition: to fall or drop straight down at high speed
exampleIELTS: Coal consumption plummeted from 60 million tonnes to barely 15 million over the period shown.

definition: to rise quickly to a high level
exampleIELTS: The number of international tourists soared, reaching a peak of 2.1 million in 2018.

definition: to stop rising or falling and remain at a steady level
exampleIELTS: After a sharp rise in the first decade, female participation plateaued at around 65%.

definition: to change frequently in size, amount, or quality
exampleIELTS: Unemployment fluctuated between 4% and 7% throughout the period, with no clear upward or downward trend.

definition: to become steady and stop changing
exampleIELTS: Carbon emissions stabilised at approximately 30 megatonnes from 2015 onwards.

definition: to reach the highest level before falling
exampleIELTS: Energy consumption peaked at 850 terawatt-hours in 2008 before declining steadily thereafter.

definition: a small, temporary fall in a level or amount
exampleIELTS: Despite a brief dip in 2015, overall production rose throughout the period.

definition: to rise gradually over time
exampleIELTS: Tuition fees climbed steadily from £3,000 in 2005 to over £9,000 by 2020.

definition: to gradually become smaller or weaker
exampleIELTS: Newspaper readership dwindled over the two decades, falling from 75% to under 30%.

definition: to a large extent or degree
exampleIELTS: The proportion of households owning a smartphone rose substantially, from 23% to 91% over the period.

definition: by a very small amount
exampleIELTS: Public transport usage rose only marginally, by about two percentage points across the decade.

definition: as judged in comparison with something else
exampleIELTS: Spending on healthcare was comparatively high, almost double that of any other category.

definition: in a way that corresponds in size or amount to something else
exampleIELTS: Although Japan's population is smaller, it consumed proportionally more energy per capita than India.

definition: by a sudden and very large amount
exampleIELTS: Renewable energy use increased dramatically, more than tripling between 2000 and 2020.

definition: at a regular and constant rate
exampleIELTS: Car ownership rose steadily across the period, gaining around two percentage points each year.

definition: suddenly and unexpectedly
exampleIELTS: The downward trend ended abruptly in 2018, when figures recovered to pre-recession levels.

definition: the lowest point in a fluctuating series of values
exampleIELTS: Sales reached a trough of just 4,000 units in 2012 before recovering throughout the rest of the decade.

definition: a part or share of a whole
exampleIELTS: A growing proportion of commuters chose cycling over driving during the period shown.

definition: a noticeable difference between two things that should match
exampleIELTS: There is a marked discrepancy between male and female enrolment in engineering, with men outnumbering women three to one.

definition: the overall pattern or path of change over time
exampleIELTS: The two countries followed a similar trajectory, with both seeing rapid urban growth after 2005.

definition: of considerable importance, size, or worth
exampleIELTS: The chart shows a substantial increase in renewable energy use between 2010 and 2020.

definition: so small or unimportant that it can be ignored
exampleIELTS: The change in coal use was negligible, varying by less than one percent across the entire period.

definition: easy to see or recognise
exampleIELTS: There was a noticeable shift towards online shopping, particularly among younger consumers.

definition: following one after another in unbroken sequence
exampleIELTS: Emissions fell for three consecutive years before rising again in the final period.

definition: to publicly recommend or support a particular policy or idea
exampleIELTS: While many advocate stricter regulation of social media, others argue that this would infringe on freedom of expression.

definition: to assert something firmly as a position in argument
exampleIELTS: Critics contend that increased automation will displace millions of low-skilled workers within a generation.

definition: to regard something as caused by a particular factor
exampleIELTS: The decline in obesity rates can largely be attributed to public health campaigns and stricter food labelling.

definition: to make a problem or bad situation worse
exampleIELTS: Banning private vehicles in city centres may exacerbate inequality, as poorer residents often live further from public transport.

definition: to make something bad less severe or harmful
exampleIELTS: Investment in renewable energy is essential if we are to mitigate the worst effects of climate change.

definition: to make a problem or suffering less intense
exampleIELTS: Conditional cash transfers have helped alleviate extreme poverty in several Latin American countries.

definition: to encourage the development of something
exampleIELTS: Schools should foster critical thinking from an early age rather than rewarding mere memorisation.

definition: to gradually weaken something, especially authority or confidence
exampleIELTS: Excessive screen time risks undermining children's ability to concentrate on extended tasks.

definition: to make something, especially a problem or belief, continue indefinitely
exampleIELTS: Stereotypes in advertising can perpetuate harmful gender norms in the workplace.

definition: to delay or make difficult the progress of something
exampleIELTS: Excessive bureaucracy continues to hinder the adoption of telemedicine in rural communities.

definition: to show or prove to be right or reasonable
exampleIELTS: Proponents argue that the financial cost of space exploration is justified by the technological spin-offs it produces.

definition: to reject something as unimportant or invalid
exampleIELTS: It would be a mistake to dismiss the concerns of parents regarding online safety simply as moral panic.

definition: to prove that a statement or theory is wrong
exampleIELTS: Recent longitudinal studies have refuted the claim that streaming services reduce attention span in adolescents.

definition: to treat something as more important than other matters
exampleIELTS: Governments should prioritise long-term environmental protection over short-term economic gains.

definition: the position or attitude one publicly takes on a matter
exampleIELTS: The author adopts a critical stance towards the privatisation of higher education.

definition: general agreement among a group
exampleIELTS: There is a clear scientific consensus that human activity is the dominant cause of recent global warming.

definition: the underlying reason or logic for a decision or belief
exampleIELTS: The rationale for taxing sugary drinks is straightforward: to discourage consumption of products linked to obesity.

definition: strongly persuasive; difficult to argue against
exampleIELTS: There is a compelling argument that universal basic income would simplify welfare and reduce administrative costs.

definition: harmful or causing damage
exampleIELTS: Excessive use of antibiotics has proven detrimental to long-term gut health in young children.

definition: certain to happen; unavoidable
exampleIELTS: Some degree of automation in the manufacturing sector now appears inevitable.

definition: more important than anything else
exampleIELTS: When designing public spaces, accessibility for people with disabilities should be paramount.

definition: having the opposite effect to the one intended
exampleIELTS: Excessively strict drug laws can be counterproductive, pushing users away from treatment programmes.

definition: possible future effects or consequences of an action
exampleIELTS: The widespread adoption of remote work has profound implications for urban housing markets.

definition: a balance between two desirable but incompatible features
exampleIELTS: There is a clear trade-off between economic growth and environmental protection in many emerging economies.

definition: to support or form the basis of an argument or system
exampleIELTS: Trust between citizens and institutions underpins every well-functioning democracy.
